summary: A ZX Spectrum tech demo by Physic, coded by Physic with music by MmcM and graphics by Diver, DMan, Zosya and Grongy. It scrolls full-screen multicolour pictures, as the opening text announces.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2023, and the source code is available.

summary: Alpha Flight's C64 birthday demo for Irata's 50th, coded by The Gothicman and Xenox with music by Celticdesign, carrying birthday messages from a long list of sceners.
why: A warm scene tribute: commenters single out the touching texts and DMD's graphics, and it's a good example of the C64 community marking one of its own.

quote.text: i like it very nice and thanks for the touchy texts.

summary: Impact's Christmas demo for the Amstrad Plus, released December 2023, with code by Demoniak and graphics by Kris.
why: A seasonal greeting from Impact that uses the Plus hardware. It's a short festive watch rather than a compo entry.

summary: The Solution's C64 demo, coded by Silpheed with graphics by Se7en and music by Xiny, placed 3rd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2018. A purple checkerboard backdrop sits behind the group logo and a scrolling message.
why: Silpheed's first C64 production after years on PS1 and Amiga. Sceners praise its style and design, Xiny's tune in particular, and a checkerboard zoom that caught people out.

quote.text: i love this, super stylish, all the music and movement comes together so nice!

summary: An MSX demo by Lieves!Tuore, with code by Marq, music by Yzi and graphics by Manu, which took second place in the demo compo at Alternative Party 1998.
why: A runner-up at Alternative Party 1998 from a Finnish group better known for other platforms, and a rare scene demo on the MSX from that era.

summary: A 512-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum 48K by Siberian Group, with sound, which came second in the ZX Spectrum 512b intro compo at CAFe 2003.
why: A second place at CAFe 2003 in one of the tightest size classes, packing both graphics and sound into 512 bytes.

summary: Dmitry_Milk's ZX Spectrum beeper demo, second in the Demo compo at DiHalt 2026 Summer, built around vocoder-style vocals over a pixel-art scene of a skeleton at a computer.
why: A Spectrum demo where the beeper, not an AY chip, carries vocoder vocals, and it placed second at DiHalt 2026 Summer.

summary: Finnish Gold's two-disk-side C64 demo, third in the Zoo 2022 demo compo, with code by Proton and Serato, music by Proton and Rock, and graphics by Pal.
why: Sceners point to the amount of top-notch code, especially the perspective scroller reflected in a ray-traced mirror ball, along with Pal's hires graphics and the mood of the disk side 2 soundtrack.
highlights: perspective scroller mirrored in a ball

quote.text: What’s not to love about this demo? Everything works perfectly together. Pal’s graphics really made me smile throughout the demo – enjoyed every plotted pixel.

summary: Singular's short C64 demo that won the Commodore Demo compo at Forever 2006, with a plasma, a wireframe object, metaballs, a picture by Leon and an upscroller ending.
why: A compact party winner. Sceners single out the smooth plasma and the nostalgic end upscroller with 1x1 and 1x2 fonts and simple ASCII art, reminiscent of old disk magazines.

quote.text: Quite smooth and good looking effects (plasma rocks!).

summary: A BBC Micro demo by Neurotypical, coded by Puppeh, that came 2nd in the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009.
why: A podium finish in a mixed oldskool compo for a BBC Micro demo, a machine that rarely turned up at demoparties at the time.

summary: A Genesis Project cracktro for the C64 by Mermaid, who did code, music and graphics alone, made in a 1988 style. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at SynchroNY 2016.
why: Sceners loved its nostalgic feel, saying it took them back to watching intros in front of games as kids, and singled out the twinkling logo and its polish.

quote.text: Brings back the time when I was a kid and was looking at these strange stuff infront of my games with wonder ^_^ A lovely release!

summary: Fraction's Commodore 64 demo from 1998, winner of the C64 demo competition at North Party 1998.
why: It took first place in the C64 demo compo at North Party 1998, a solid late-nineties showing from Fraction.

summary: Lethargy's two-disk-side C64 demake of Gargaj's PC demo Median, placing 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2021. This is the party version, built with the Sparkle loader.
why: Sceners praise its fresh, animated design and tight sync, and many didn't realise it was a port until told. Even those who did called it a seriously impressive conversion that shows how much design space is left on the C64.

quote.text: Superb demo! It's fantastic to see how animated demos with great concepts take the whole idea of demo art to another level!

summary: Inka's Game Boy Color demo, second in the Console Demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2002, with code by Lai, music by Psychad and graphics by Gaxar and Zaphod. The video is captured from a real handheld.
why: A podium finish in the console compo at one of the big German parties of its day, and a chance to see the work running on real Game Boy Color hardware rather than an emulator.

summary: Ilmenit's 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari 256b intro compo at Lost Party 2020. It moves through generated patterns, from a Sierpinski triangle to fanned colour stripes and layered hills.
why: A compo winner that fits several distinct generated scenes and sound into 256 bytes. The source is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: Realm Of Illusion's Vectrex demo, coded by Frog with music by C-jeff and voice by Random. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2015.
why: A rare demo for the Vectrex's vector display. Its Solskogen compo entry makes it a good chance to see what the machine can do in scene hands.

summary: Ancient runes is a ZX Spectrum demo by Q-Bone, released in 2017. It came second in the LowEnd Demo competition at DiHalt 2017.
why: A second place in DiHalt 2017's LowEnd Demo compo makes it a solid example of Spectrum demo work from that year's Russian party scene.
highlights: dithered textures shifting beside the artwork

summary: Orange's first Commodore 64 demo and the third part of their Television series, with code by Galvados, music by Zardax and graphics by Der Piipo and Jate.
why: An Amiga group's long-awaited arrival on the C64. Sceners single out the subpixel rigid-body physics and antialiasing, Zardax's bass-heavy tune and the final Orange logo.

quote.text: Loving subpixel rigid body physics and antialiasing (shown for a bit too short though!). Final logo piece is outstanding too.

summary: ThePetsMode's MSX1 demo, placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019, with code from JamQue, Napalm, Fubu and Mvac7 and music by JosSs.
why: A recent MSX1 group demo that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Revision, with several coders and graphicians pooling their work.

summary: Padua's C64 trackmo that won the Trackmo compo at BCC Party 2020, with code by Dano and Doomed, music by Toggle and graphics by Jailbird, Twoflower, Shine and Cupid.
why: Sceners call it fast-paced, with a good variety of parts. They single out the cube part, the vortex and Toggle's tune, and praise how familiar effects get their own twist and are glued into one stylish demo.

quote.text: Yes, lots of parts we’ve seen in other productions - but you’ve brought something to each one to glue them together into a very cool demo.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Flush, with code by flewww, graphics by Exocet and music by Glafouk. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2018.
why: A size-limited intro on one of the most constrained machines around, and it made the podium at Revision. The source is released under the GPL for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Visac and LHS that placed 4th in the Demo compo at Árok 2011. The video, filmed off the party screen, calls it a 4K intro.
why: A small Plus/4 entry from the Hungarian Árok party, shown here as the audience saw it on the big screen.

summary: Abyss-Connection's C64 anniversary slideshow marking the group's 20 years, with pictures by six graphicians and music by FieserWolf. It placed 5th in Alternative Platforms at Evoke 2011.
why: Sceners praise the pictures, FieserWolf's music and the way the bitmaps fade in and out. One singles out the screen being reinstalled at the end.

quote.text: Very cool demo, I like the way the bitmaps fade, the music and art here is fantastic also!

summary: A Vectrex 64K intro and invitation by the Carnegie Mellon University Computer Club, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at @Party 2019.
why: A first-place compo winner on the Vectrex, a vector-display console rarely seen in demo competitions.

summary: New Generation and Zelax's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k22 SE, with code by Święty, Yosh, Solo and Laoo and music by Miker, ZoltarX and Tatqoo.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, made by a large crew of coders, musicians and graphicians. It needs a machine expanded to 512K.

summary: Beyond Force's C64 demo from Light and Phenomena Easter Party 1992, where it came second in the demo compo. Coded by Gremlin, Sam and Tnt, it opens with a text flasher over a 3D starfield.
why: Billed by its makers as the first palindromic demo on the C64 (read the title backwards), and a runner-up at a major Swedish party of the time.

summary: EXclusive ON's C64 demo, which came third in the C64 demo compo at North Party 2006. Volcano coded it, with graphics by Jammer, Bedrich and Sunset and music by Jammer.
why: Sceners single out the hires graphics and fast realtime effects, and several felt it deserved a higher placing; it was shown unfinished at the party.

quote.text: the hires gfx are really good

summary: Alone 34 is a ZX Spectrum demo by mayHem and Skrju, released in December 2015 for the enhanced Spectrum models.
why: A joint release between mayHem and Skrju. There are no compo results, notes or comments on record, so the video is the best guide to it.

summary: Triad's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2008, built on a monochrome, heavily distorted look with bouncing balls, sine screens and transforming letters.
why: Sceners credit its daring, original style and hypnotic, looping atmosphere, and enjoyed seeing effects revived that hadn't been used for a decade. The bouncing balls on the sine screen are the most-praised part.
highlights: balls bouncing on a sine screen

quote.text: Mesmerizing! Hypnotic! And quite original, too! That style, the looping tune (and demo). I found myself watching it two times in a row

summary: Dragon Software Productions' C64 demo from 2000, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000. Code by Fenek and Wedlock, music by Praiser and Sage.
why: Sceners praise its music and the way the parts' mood fits it. Coders credit Fenek with an early "2nd Pixel FLI" mode that later prods such as The Larch borrowed from.

quote.text: Somehow the music and the feeling of the parts fitted so well together, and the now dated design was really creative.

summary: A joint Amstrad CPC demo by Hardos, Vanity, Benediction, Shinra and Dentifrice, coded by Krusty with music by PulkoMandy, which placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2024.
why: A multi-group CPC collaboration with a deep graphics roster in Voxy, Slyder and Exocet, plus Beb on rasters, that competed at Revision, one of the biggest demoparties.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Arkos from 1999, with code, design and music by Targhan and an end part drawn by Toms.
why: A largely one-person production: Targhan handled the code, design and music himself. Worth a look for anyone exploring late-1990s CPC demos.

summary: The Megademo is a 1988 Commodore 64 megademo by Higher Intelligence Company: a run of parts with scrolling messages, raster bars and a drummer part with a digitised tune.
why: Sceners remember it as one of the first megademos they saw and still rate it highly. They single out the music throughout, the raster bars and the drummer whose hands are synchronised with the audio.

quote.text: the guy playing drums is so cool: synchronized audio with the guy's hands. And also the drum the guy beats on changes accoring to the played drum.

summary: Gordian's minimalist 16K intro for the C64, with music by Jammer and a font by Tao, that won the C64 intro compo at Xenium 2025: white dots gather, scatter and orbit around a single ball.
why: Sceners praise its minimalism, its originality and how well Jammer's music fits, with several comparing it to watching a short film. Coders singled out the plotting trick of sharing dynamically built characters between dots.

quote.text: A visually minimal impression that becomes something truly enormous in the mind.

summary: Marquee Design's 256-byte procedural graphics prod for the Atari XE/XL, which won the oldskool procedural graphics compo at Lovebyte 2024. It draws a faceted pink seahorse against a banded blue underwater backdrop.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2024, packing a recognisable underwater scene into 256 bytes of code.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Amstrad CPC by Overflow, placed 5th in the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2024.
why: A compact size-coding entry from a dedicated tiny-intro party, showing how much screen activity fits into 256 bytes on the CPC.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by g0blinish, with music by Ahim, that placed third in the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2020.
why: A podium finish at Demosplash 2020's retro compo. It's a small one-coder Spectrum production that asks, in its own words, whether demomaking makes sense.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Gemba Boys, with code from Noby, Busy, UB880D, Logout and Poke and graphics by Noby, Logout and Trixs. It came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2011.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2011 made by a group of well-known Slovak Spectrum coders, with each part credited on screen to its author along a status bar.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Resource, coded by Oswald, Edhellon and Blala with graphics by Poison and music by Jammer. It came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2024.
why: A second place at Revision's Oldskool 4K Intro compo, against entries from every classic platform, makes it a good look at what a modern team can fit into 4K on the Plus 4.

summary: Da Boxon Team's Amstrad Plus intro, coded by Nicky One with graphics by Bouba and music by Giherem. It came second in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #4 in 2024.
why: A comeback release: the scroller says it arrives 26 years after the group's last demo, made for the CPC fans who kept the scene going. It took second place at Benediction Coding Party #4.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by superogue, released under Marquee Design's channel, that placed second in the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2021.
why: A second place at DiHalt 2021 for an intro of just 256 bytes that includes sound, coded and designed by superogue alone.

summary: A 2K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Benediction, coded by Eliot with music by Warlord, which placed third in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #6 in 2026.
why: A compo placer that packs a scene and a soundtrack into 2K, with Voxfreax credited for the palette work.
highlights: sky colours that shift through palettes

summary: Sage's Atari Lynx demo, coded by Sage with graphics by Flash and Lowlife, which placed second in the Intro compo at Error In Line 2003.
why: The notes bill it as showing effects never seen on the Lynx before, including HiColor graphics beyond the handheld's usual 16 colours, set to a digital soundtrack.

summary: A C64 demo by Funkentstört, with code by Kometbomb and graphics and music by Ilkke and Animal Bro, placed 3rd in the Oldschool demo compo at Flashback 2014. A cartoon cat sits over a patterned backdrop while text scrolls beneath.
why: Sceners single out the catchy, stuttering tune and the cute cat art, with one wishing there had been more of it.

quote.text: That stuttering tune is so catchy.

summary: Genesis Project's wintry C64 graphics demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2020: a slideshow of hires pictures by Mermaid, Shadow and Redcrab with scrolltexts and music by Zyron.
why: Sceners praise the warm, nostalgic artwork and the smoothly animated sprite scarf above all, along with the parallax landscape and the scrolltexts. Several thought it deserved a higher placing.

quote.text: This is really a demo, which easily could be shown to almost all kinds of audience outside the nerdy c64 kit and be appreciated.

summary: Overflow's 256-byte intro for the Amstrad CPC, placed 6th in the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2024.
why: A compact size-coding entry from a recent Lovebyte, and a writeup is available for anyone curious how it fits in 256 bytes.

summary: A 1991 Amstrad CPC demo coded by Elmsoft Game Service: a figure walks across a chequerboard floor beneath big colour-gradient scrolltexts, with an on-screen "Demo time left" countdown.
why: A thin fact sheet with no compo history or comments, but a period CPC demo that pairs vector and ball-built 3D figures with raster colour scrolling in a single scene.

summary: A Christmas-themed Amstrad CPC demo by Arkos from 1997, with code by Targhan, Orphée and Rainbird, graphics by Rainbird, and music from Targhan, Tom&Jerry and Rob Hubbard.
why: An Arkos group effort from the French CPC scene of the late 1990s, warmly received on Pouët. It is tagged nsfw, so expect some content not for every audience.

summary: SquoQuo's Atari 8-bit intro, which won the size-limited realtime compo at Demodays 2014. A SquoQuo logo and scrolling text messages sit over a cyan checkerboard.
why: A compo winner at Demodays 2014, with code by Hopper, music by 505 and graphics by Widdy and Raven.

summary: An MSX2 demo by N.I from 2017, built around a single pixel-art picture of an anime-style girl in an MSX-branded sailor top, wired up with cables.
why: A small one-picture demo that leans on the MSX2's palette. The same drawing is recoloured through very different schemes over its run.
